findings.summary: docs/planning/v1.2.md line 30 still lists F3/F4/F6/F7/F8 as 'remain Open'; pre-existing and not a current-state surface, so not required by 20.3.
findings.detail: The accepted plan document states 'F3, F4, F6, F7, and F8 are promoted to v1.2 by this plan and remain **Open** until their resolving phase lands and records the resolution.' Phases 15, 17, and 19 resolved F8, F3, and F4/F6 without editing this sentence, so the staleness is a pre-existing pattern in the accepted-plan artifact (docs/INDEX.md class 'Plan': the accepted release/scope plan), not something 20.3 introduced or is scoped to fix. The statement is a conditional rule ('until their resolving phase lands and records the resolution') and therefore remains literally true, whereas PLANS.md's claim that F4/F6/F7 'remain **Open**' was a false current-state assertion and was correctly corrected. A grep across current-state surfaces (PLANS.md, docs/status.md, docs/limitations/*) shows no remaining F7-open claim. No change required; recorded so a later documentation pass does not read this as an omission by 20.3.
evidence: git log --oneline: F8/F3/F4/F6 resolutions committed in earlier phases without editing that sentence
grep -rn 'F7' --include=*.md: no 'F7 ... Open' claim on PLANS.md, docs/status.md, or docs/limitations/
findings.recommended_action: No action for 20.3. Optionally reconcile the accepted plan's conditional sentence in the Phase 21 canonical documentation reconciliation task if that document is treated as current-state.

findings.summary: The worker report's probe description names CandidateAfterPresence as the removed guard; the resume entry's guard is on operation.SourcePresence (the shared mutation branch does read CandidateAfterPresence).
findings.detail: Worker-report.json validation[2] and test_sensitivity[0] describe changing ResumeRestorationAsync so that 'CandidateAfterPresence == Absent' fell into the present-baseline artifact-read branch. In the shipped code, ResumeRestorationAsync reads the retained artifact under `if (operation.SourcePresence == ArtworkImagePresence.Present)` (src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:860-874), while the shared ExecuteRestorationAsync mutation branch keys on `operation.CandidateAfterPresence` (lines 730-733, 756). Because the new test seeds both fields as Absent, either description produces the same probe result, and I independently reproduced the claimed outcome (Failed 1, Passed 25, Total 26; Expected Completed / Actual RecoveryBlocked) by removing the SourcePresence guard in an isolated copy. The imprecision is confined to a historical report sentence and changes no conclusion.
findings.recommended_action: No action; historical report text is immutable.

verified_requirements.requirement: Deliverable 2 - architecture/09 coordinator-attributed removal wording corrected without overclaim
verified_requirements.detail: I verified the mechanism in source rather than the prose. ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.ReadRetainedSource (line 328) returns RetainedSourceResolution.Failed(ArtworkSourceReadResult.Absent(...)) when state.SourcePresence == Absent (lines 345-349), and GenerateCoreAsync (line 209) returns ArtworkGenerationResult.NoSource on ArtworkSourceReadStatus.Absent (lines 213-218) before RenderAsync (line 238) and before the pass-through branch that calls RestoreEmptySelectionAsync (line 247). So the coordinator cannot create an absent-baseline restoration, and the amended architecture text (docs/architecture/09:274-283) states exactly that, attributes the removal to the publisher, names the two places the leg is exercised (publisher fresh test from 20.2 and the recovery-gate resume added here), and does not claim a coordinator path. The 'publishes only a Rendered result' clause was also corrected to name the owned empty-selection restore obligation, matching the shipped branch. The note does not overclaim: it states the unreachability rather than asserting coverage of a leg that does not exist.
